evidence: Sen. Ep. 63.2: etiam Niobam dē cibō cōgitāsse
Cic. Off. 1.105: mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō
terms.comment: With dē and the ablative for what one thinks about (dē tē cōgitō), an accusative, or a question (quid agam cōgitō). With an infinitive it means “intend” (see mean, intend).

evidence: Ter. Eun. 591: Dum haec mēcum reputō
terms.comment: Mostly with sēcum or cum animō: turning something over in one’s mind.

phrases.latin: aedificāre diū cōgitāre oportet, cōnserere cōgitāre nōn oportet, sed facere oportet
phrases.english: Building you should think about for a long time; planting you shouldn’t think about: you should just do it.

phrases.latin: cum dīxerit etiam Niobam dē cibō cōgitāsse
phrases.english: since Homer said that even Niobe thought about food

sources: Lewis & Short: cogito · Lewis & Short: reputo
